html:
Jamaica is a Caribbean island south of Cuba. Its first people were the Taíno. Spain settled it in 1509, and England seized it in 1655. Its port of Port Royal became a base for buccaneers until an earthquake sank much of the town in 1692.

Under British rule Jamaica became a great sugar island, worked by Africans brought through the Atlantic slave trade. Escaped slaves, the Maroons, held the mountains and forced Britain into treaties in 1739. The Baptist War of 1831 hastened the end of slavery in the British Empire. After the Morant Bay rebellion of 1865 Britain ruled the island directly.

Labour riots in 1938 gave birth to the trade unions and parties that led Jamaica to independence in 1962. The island's influence is far larger than its size: Marcus Garvey was born here, Rastafari began here, and Bob Marley took reggae around the world.
